content.comment_body: Hello everyone, My old [product_name] stopped working, so I installed a new one that currently has no program loaded. I now need to set it up manually since I don’t have any programming software available. I’m trying to configure it so that input “I1” will trigger output “Q1”, or have a timer make “Q1” activate every two hours for three seconds, then repeat the countdown. I realize I need an “OR” logic block, but I’m unsure what else is required to make Q1 turn on every two hours for three seconds. For experienced users, this may be simple, but as a first-time user, I’m finding the interface a bit confusing. Any guidance would be greatly appreciated.

You can download the programming software for this [product_name]. There’s a demo version available which allows you to create and simulate your program on your PC, but you won’t be able to transfer it to the device. The simulation is quite useful, so you can test your logic before deploying it. Programming can also be done directly on the device screen if the logic isn’t very complex. The [company_name] website offers free web-based lessons explaining how to use and program the [product_name]. All you need to invest is your time.

I understand, and having the software would indeed be helpful. However, I’m currently on a ship with extremely slow internet access — it took me 35 minutes just to download a small user manual. That’s why I’m still looking for alternative solutions and appreciate any support.
Solved it, thanks to my own efforts. This thread can be closed.

Here’s a possible solution: Navigate to the output settings for Q1. Use the down arrow six times until you see 'asynchronous.' Set En to I1 (input 1), then proceed to Par and enter your desired times for activation and deactivation. Confirm and exit the program, then start it. Give this a try; it may work for your needs. If you’re interested, I have a thread on similar timing issues you can check for more details.

The asynchronous pulse generator is one of the available functions in [product_name] programming. It includes an enable input, output, and parameter settings. When enabled, it will output a pulse according to your chosen parameters. You can set how long the output remains active (time high) and inactive (time low). The pulse shape at the output is customizable with a pulse/pause ratio. When the enable input is triggered, the pulse generator toggles the output on and off based on these time settings.
Thank you for your help. I managed to resolve the issue myself using the asynchronous pulse generator, and everything is functioning correctly.

analysis.insight_summary: Users face difficulties manually programming the [product_name] when programming software is inaccessible, particularly in situations with limited internet connectivity such as on ships. Beginners find identifying and configuring logic blocks, like the asynchronous pulse generator, less intuitive. Despite these challenges, self-guided programming using the device’s interface and available documentation allows users to achieve their automation goals without external software, although the process may be less efficient.
analysis.user_expectations: The user hopes for a straightforward method to program the [product_name] manually, without relying on external software, desiring to easily set up timer-based and input-activated operations through the device interface.
